subject: conditional vs full likelihood with sessions with no captures

messages.author: 5385d987d753e1aa
messages.subject: conditional vs full likelihood with sessions with no captures
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to model a large dataset with a few sessions that have no captures. Using a subset of the data (including sessions with no captures) and the full likelihood works great. However, I would prefer to use the conditional likelihood for speed. When I run the same model that worked for the full likelihood with the conditional likelihood instead of getting an estimate of density for the session with no captures I get NAs.

Is it possible to use the conditional likelihood with sessions with no captures? If so, how?

Thanks,
Alex

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: conditional vs full likelihood with sessions with no captures
parts: I think the answer is 'no'. Presumably the best estimate is zero? The conditional likelihood density estimate is a Horvitz-Thompson-like estimate, essentially the sum of the reciprocals of per-capita effective sampling areas, one for each detected animal. If there are no detected animals then derived() has nothing to work with. One could extrapolate the denominator (effective sampling area) from somewhere else and set a numerator of zero, but what's the point?
